proposals.before: In spring of the first year of the Xianhe era (326), on the dinghai day of the second month, the court proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the new reign title, ordered five days of public feasting, distributed a hu of grain each to widowers, widows, orphans, and the elderly, and remitted one year of taxes and labor service within a hundred li of the capital.
proposals.after: In spring of the first year of the Xianhe era (326), on the dinghai day of the second month, the court proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the new reign title, ordered five days of public feasting, distributed rice to widowers, widows, orphans, and the elderly at the rate of one hu for every two persons, and remitted one year of taxes and labor service within a hundred li of the capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 二人斛 means one hu for two persons, not one hu each; the idiomatic rendering invents an equal per-person ration.

proposals.before: On the guihai day of the sixth month Liu Xia, duke of Quanling—holder of the insignia of authority, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, supervisor of all forces north of the Huai, north gentlemans-household general, and inspector of Xuzhou—passed away.
proposals.after: On the guihai day of the sixth month Liu Xia, duke of Quanling—holder of the insignia of authority, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, supervisor of all forces north of the Huai, General of the North Gentlemen of the Household, and inspector of Xuzhou—passed away.
proposals.reason: English gentlemans is ungrammatical for 北中郎將 and obscures the office name.

proposals.before: On the guiyou day Xi Jian, general of chariots and cavalry, was ordered to take charge of Xuzhou as well, while Guo Mo, general who conquers the caitiffs, was named north gentlemans-household general, granted the credential staff, and put in command of the armies north of the Huai.
proposals.after: On the guiyou day Xi Jian, general of chariots and cavalry, was ordered to take charge of Xuzhou as well, while Guo Mo, general who conquers the caitiffs, was named General of the North Gentlemen of the Household, granted the credential staff, and put in command of the armies north of the Huai.
proposals.reason: Same ungrammatical gentlemans for 北中郎將 as in the preceding unit.

proposals.before: Borrowed Guard General Yu Liang's staff as campaign area commander, made Right Guard General Zhao Yin Champion General, Administrator of Liyang, ordered together with Left General Sima Liu to lead troops to resist Jun, battled at Cihu, Liu was defeated, died in it.
proposals.after: Yu Liang, Guard General, was granted the ceremonial staff as campaign commander-in-chief; Right Guard General Zhao Yin was made Champion General and Administrator of Liyang and, together with Left General Sima Liu, ordered to lead troops to resist Jun; they battled at Cihu; Liu was defeated and died in that battle.
proposals.reason: 假…節 means conferring the ceremonial staff of command, not borrowing Yu Liang's staff.

proposals.before: Borrowed Agile Cavalry General Zhong Ya's staff, led boat army, with Zhao Yin as van, in order to resist Jun.
proposals.after: Agile Cavalry General Zhong Ya was granted the ceremonial staff and led the boat army, with Zhao Yin as the van, in order to resist Jun.
proposals.reason: 假…節 is a grant of the jie staff of command, not borrowing Zhong Ya's staff.

proposals.before: In the first month of spring in the third year of Xianhe (328), Wen Qiao, general who pacifies the south, moved upstream to relieve the capital and halted at Xunyang, dispatching Wang Yanqi, Deng Yue of Xiyang, and Ji Mu of Poyang as his vanguard commanders.
proposals.after: In the first month of spring in the third year of Xianhe (328), Wen Qiao, general who pacifies the south, led troops to relieve the capital and halted at Xunyang, dispatching Wang Yanqi, Deng Yue of Xiyang, and Ji Mu of Poyang as his vanguard commanders.
proposals.reason: 帥師救京師 does not say he moved upstream; that direction is an invention.

proposals.before: Third year spring first month, General Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao led troops to rescue the capital, halted at Xunyang, sent Supervisors Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue, Administrator of Poyang Ji Mu as van.
proposals.after: Third year spring first month, General Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao led troops to rescue the capital, halted at Xunyang, sent Supervisor Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue, and Administrator of Poyang Ji Mu as van.
proposals.reason: 督護 applies to Wang Yanqi only; Deng Yue and Ji Mu are commandery administrators, so Supervisors should not be pluralized across all three.

proposals.before: On the gengxu day of the second month Su Jun reached Mount Jiang east of the capital.
proposals.after: On the gengxu day of the second month Su Jun reached Mount Jiang.
proposals.reason: 蔣山 is named without locating it east of the capital; that gloss is added.

proposals.before: Borrowed General Who Commands the Army Bian Kun's staff, led six armies, and with Jun battled at Xiling, royal army was greatly defeated.
proposals.after: General Who Commands the Army Bian Kun was granted the ceremonial staff, led the six armies, and battled Jun at Xiling; the royal army was greatly defeated.
proposals.reason: 假…節 is a grant of the jie staff, not borrowing Bian Kun's staff.

proposals.before: On the renshen day Empress Mingmu was interred beside Emperor Ming at the Wuping mausoleum.
proposals.after: On the renshen day Empress Mingmu was interred at the Wuping mausoleum.
proposals.reason: The Chinese says only 葬明穆皇后于武平陵 and does not mention Emperor Ming or burial beside him.

proposals.before: On the yiwei day of the fifth month Su Jun forced the emperor to relocate to his stronghold at Stone Fort; the boy sovereign wept as he boarded the cart, and lamentation filled the palace.
proposals.after: On the yiwei day of the fifth month Su Jun forced the emperor to relocate to his stronghold at Stone Fort; the emperor wept as he boarded the cart, and lamentation filled the palace.
proposals.reason: 帝 does not call him a boy; 'boy sovereign' is an added characterization.

proposals.before: In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Xianhe (329), while the emperor remained at Stone Fort, the rebel general Kuang Shu surrendered the Yuan walled park, and the court officials flocked to rejoin him.
proposals.after: In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Xianhe (329), while the emperor remained at Stone Fort, the rebel general Kuang Shu surrendered the Yuan walled park, and the court officials flocked there.
proposals.reason: 百官赴焉 points to the surrendered Yuan City (焉), not to rejoining Kuang Shu personally.

proposals.before: An edict restored three years of rent and tax to commanderies and counties that had suffered bandits.
proposals.after: An edict remitted three years of rent and tax for commanderies and counties that had suffered bandits.
proposals.reason: 復 here is tax remission for ravaged counties, not restoration of collections.

proposals.before: Eighth month, Li Yao's generals Liu Yin and others led troops to invade Shi Sheng and halted at Yong.
proposals.after: Eighth month, Liu Yao's generals Liu Yin and others led troops to invade Shi Sheng and halted at Yong (received 利 is a corruption of 劉).
proposals.reason: 利曜 is the corrupted graph for 劉曜; rendering Li Yao as a separate surname misstates the referent.

proposals.before: In the eighth month of autumn Shi Le declared himself emperor of Zhao and dispatched Guo Jing against Xiangyang.
proposals.after: In the eighth month of autumn Shi Le usurped the imperial throne and dispatched Guo Jing against Xiangyang.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 僭卽皇帝位 does not name Zhao; the idiomatic English invents 'emperor of Zhao' and softens 僭 'usurped'.

proposals.before: Zhou Fu, south gentlemans-household general, fell back to Wuchang, and the refugees from the central plains submitted en masse to Shi Le.
proposals.after: Zhou Fu, South Gentlemen of the Household General, fell back to Wuchang, and the refugees from the central plains submitted en masse to Shi Le.
proposals.reason: gentlemans is ungrammatical; 南中郎將 is the office South Gentlemen of the Household General.

proposals.before: Li Shou, a general under Li Xiong of Cheng, struck Badong and Jianping, forcing army supervisor Wuqiu Ao and Prefect Yang Qian to withdraw to Yidu.
proposals.after: Li Shou, a general under Li Xiong, struck Badong and Jianping, forcing army supervisor Wuqiu Ao and Prefect Yang Qian to withdraw to Yidu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 李雄將李壽 does not name the Cheng state; 'of Cheng' is an added polity not in the source sentence.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month Zhang Jun of Former Liang acknowledged Shi Le as overlord.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month Zhang Jun acknowledged Shi Le as overlord.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 張駿稱臣于石勒 does not mention Former Liang; the polity name is invented in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: In the third month Zhao Yin, west gentlemans-household general, and Kuang Shu, a staff gentleman of the minister of education, stormed Shi Le's riverside stronghold at Matou and took it.
proposals.after: In the third month Zhao Yin, West Gentlemen of the Household General, and Kuang Shu, a staff gentleman of the minister of education, stormed Shi Le's riverside stronghold at Matou and took it.
proposals.reason: gentlemans is ungrammatical in the office rendering of 西中郎將.

proposals.before: Tao Kan, grand commandant, sent his son Tao Bin, an adviser on the staff of the general who pacifies the west, and Huan Xuan, south gentlemans-household general, against Guo Jing. They broke his army and took Fancheng.
proposals.after: Tao Kan, grand commandant, sent his son Tao Bin, an adviser on the staff of the general who pacifies the west, and Huan Xuan, South Gentlemen of the Household General, against Guo Jing. They broke his army and took Fancheng.
proposals.reason: gentlemans is ungrammatical in the office rendering of 南中郎將.

proposals.before: On the wuchen day of the seventh month Shi Le died. His son Shi Hong inherited the Zhao throne, while general Shi Cong brought the district of Qiao over to Jin.
proposals.after: On the wuchen day of the seventh month Shi Le died. His son Shi Hong inherited the false throne, while general Shi Cong brought the district of Qiao over to Jin.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 嗣偽位 does not name Zhao; 'the Zhao throne' replaces the source's 'false throne'.

proposals.before: In the fourth month of summer Shi Hu sent Shi Bin against Guo Quan at Mei and reduced the town.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of summer Shi Hong's general Shi Hu sent Shi Bin against Guo Quan at Mei and captured the town.
proposals.reason: Chinese 石弘將石季龍 makes Shi Hu Shi Hong's general; the idiomatic sentence drops Shi Hong and that command relation.

proposals.before: In the eleventh month Shi Hu murdered Shi Hong and proclaimed himself heavenly king of Zhao.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month Shi Hu murdered Shi Hong and established himself as Heavenly King.
proposals.reason: Chinese 自立爲天王 does not name Zhao; the polity is interpolated.

proposals.before: On the jiazi day of the second month the emperor personally offered the capping sacrifice to Confucius.
proposals.after: On the jiazi day of the second month the emperor personally performed the libation offering.
proposals.reason: 釋奠 is the school libation rite; Confucius is not named in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Shi Yu, serving Shi Hu, struck Zhonglu, and Wang Guo, south gentlemans-household general, fell back to defend Xiangyang.
proposals.after: Shi Yu, serving Shi Hu, struck Zhonglu, and Wang Guo, General of the Household Gentlemen of the South, fell back to defend Xiangyang.
proposals.reason: south gentlemans-household general is ungrammatical for 南中郎將.

proposals.before: Second month, reckoning military-use tax rice, empty suspended more than five hundred thousand shi, from Masters of Writing Xie Bao si downward dismissed from office.
proposals.after: Second month, reckoning military-use tax rice, empty suspended more than five hundred thousand shi; from Masters of Writing Xie Bao downward, dismissed from office.
proposals.reason: 巳下 is the variant writing of 已下 “and those below,” not a name element si.

proposals.before: The cadet branches of the Ji surname were enfeoffed to guard the Zhou royal house, a grace recorded in splendor on the Han rolls.
proposals.after: The cadet Ji were enfeoffed in Wei, a grace recorded in splendor on the Han rolls.
proposals.reason: 宗姬侯衛 points to Ji cadets enfeoffed as Wei, matching the later 衛公; the idiomatic expansion to guarding the Zhou house is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: In the sixth month the office of minister of education was retitled chancellor, and Grand Tutor Wang Dao was appointed to the post; the particle meaning by appointment was miscopied as the graph for second heavenly stem.
proposals.after: In the sixth month the office of minister of education was retitled chancellor, and Grand Tutor Wang Dao was appointed to the post.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English interpolates a textual-critical note about 乙/以 that is not a translation of the sentence.

proposals.before: Sixth month, changed Minister of Education to Chancellor, yi Grand Tutor Wang Dao was it.
proposals.after: Sixth month, changed Minister of Education to Chancellor, and took Grand Tutor Wang Dao to fill it.
proposals.reason: 乙 is the graphic error for 以 ‘take/use as’; the literal line is otherwise unintelligible.

proposals.before: On the gengshen day of the seventh month Wang Dao, duke of Shian—credential-bearing palace attendant, chancellor, and inspector of Yangzhou—died.
proposals.after: On the gengshen day of the seventh month Wang Dao, duke of Shixing—credential-bearing palace attendant, chancellor, and inspector of Yangzhou—died.
proposals.reason: 始興 is Shixing, not Shian.

proposals.before: Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor, concurrent Inspector of Yangzhou, Duke of Shian Wang Dao died.
proposals.after: Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor, concurrent Inspector of Yangzhou, Duke of Shixing Wang Dao died.
proposals.reason: 始興 is Shixing, not Shian.

proposals.before: Kui An withdrew but swept through eastern Hanzhong, deporting more than seven thousand households to the You and Ji regions.
proposals.after: Kui An withdrew but swept through the country east of the Han, deporting more than seven thousand households to the You and Ji regions.
proposals.reason: 漢東 is east of the Han River, not Hanzhong.

proposals.before: In the third month Empress Yang the martyr was for the first time given joint offerings in Emperor Wu's temple.
proposals.after: In the third month the Wudao Empress Yang was for the first time given joint offerings in Emperor Wu's temple.
proposals.reason: 武悼 is a posthumous title (Martial Lament), not ‘martyr’.

proposals.before: Summer, sixth month, day gengyin, the emperor was unwell; an edict stated, "He, with small years, had inherited the great continuation, been entrusted above kings and dukes, and reigned now eighteen years.
proposals.after: Summer, sixth month, day gengyin, the emperor was unwell; an edict stated, "I, with small years, had inherited the great continuation, been entrusted above kings and dukes, and reigned now eighteen years.
proposals.reason: 朕 is first person; rendering it as ‘He’ reverses the voice of the edict.

proposals.before: Prince Yue of Langye, minister of education, is my mother's brother, mature in kindness, with the bearing of a true ruler, and he commands the confidence of the age.
proposals.after: Prince Yue of Langye, minister of education, is my younger brother by the same mother, mature in kindness, with the bearing of a true ruler, and he commands the confidence of the age.
proposals.reason: 母弟 means younger brother by the same mother, not maternal uncle.

proposals.before: Minister of Education, Prince of Langye Yue, in kinship then mother's younger brother, in substance then benevolent and senior, lord-of-men's air, truly fills the age's hope.
proposals.after: Minister of Education, Prince of Langye Yue, in kinship then younger brother by the same mother, in substance then benevolent and senior, lord-of-men's air, truly fills the age's hope.
proposals.reason: 母弟 is uterine younger brother; ‘mother's younger brother’ is English for 舅.

proposals.before: He had known nothing of the execution of Prince Zong of Nandun. After Su Jun fell he asked Yu Liang, "Where is the white-haired lord he used to see at court?"
proposals.after: He had known nothing of the execution of Prince Zong of Nandun. After Su Jun fell he asked Yu Liang, "Where is the white-haired lord who was always spoken of?"
proposals.reason: 常曰 is ‘always said/spoken of’; the translation invents seeing him at court.

proposals.before: In the fourth month of summer Zhou Fu, inspector of Yizhou, and Cao Ju, prefect of Xiyang, attacked Li Shou and routed one of his generals at Jiangyang; the name in the text may stand for Huan.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of summer Zhou Fu, inspector of Yizhou, and Cao Ju, prefect of Xiyang, attacked Li Shou and routed his general Heng at Jiangyang.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the named general 恆 and inserts an unsourced conjecture that the graph stands for 桓.

proposals.before: The edict closed. Shi Hu then marched against Murong Huang and was crushingly defeated.
proposals.after: Shi Hu marched against Murong Huang and was crushingly defeated.
proposals.reason: The Chinese unit is only the Shi Hu–Murong Huang campaign; 'The edict closed' and 'then' are translator glue not in the source.

proposals.before: Huan Wen, general who supports the state and interior secretary of Langye, was named junior van commander of the van, given the credential staff, and ordered into Linhuai with his troops. Yu Yi, general who pacifies the west, became grand campaign commander-in-chief and shifted his headquarters to Xiangyang.
proposals.after: Huan Wen, general who supports the state and interior secretary of Langye, was named junior van commander, given the credential staff, and ordered into Linhuai with his troops. Yu Yi, general who pacifies the west, became grand campaign commander-in-chief and shifted his headquarters to Xiangyang.
proposals.reason: 前鋒小督 is one office; 'of the van' repeats 前鋒 and obscures the title.

proposals.before: In the first month of spring in the second year of Jianyuan, Zhang Jun dispatched He Lin and Xie Ai against the Southern Qiang in the Khotan region and shattered them.
proposals.after: In the first month of spring in the second year of Jianyuan, Zhang Jun dispatched He Lin and Xie Ai against the Southern Qiang at Tianhe and shattered them.
proposals.reason: 于闐和 uses locative 于 plus place 闐和; rendering it as the Khotan region (于闐) invents a Tarim identification the wording does not require.

proposals.before: In the fourth month Zhang Guan, serving Zhang Jun, defeated Wang Zhuo of Zhao at Sanjiao city.
proposals.after: In the fourth month Zhang Guan, serving Zhang Jun, defeated Shi Hu's general Wang Zhuo at Sanjiao city.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Wang Zhuo as 石季龍將, not as a man 'of Zhao'; Zhao is an unsourced interpolation.

proposals.before: Initially, when Emperor Cheng was ill, Palace Secretariat Director Yu Bing, considering himself maternal uncle clan holding court, power equal to the lord of men, feared after a different generation, affinal kin would become distant, then said the state had strong enemies, ought to establish a senior lord, thereupon took the emperor as heir.
proposals.after: Initially, when Emperor Cheng was ill, Palace Secretariat Director Yu Bing, considering that as the maternal-uncle house he held the court and that his power equaled the sovereign's, feared that after a change of generations the affinal kin would be distanced; he then said the state had strong enemies and that a mature ruler ought to be established, and thereupon took the emperor as heir.
proposals.reason: The literal English is ungrammatical and fuses 舅氏當朝 into 'maternal uncle clan holding court,' obscuring that Yu Bing's maternal-uncle house dominated court with power rivaling the throne.

proposals.before: Had not armies worthy of Duke Wen of Jin rallied the imperial carriage, and had the dynasty not been tethered like the mulberry at its roots, it would have owed everything to Lord Tao Kan's might.
proposals.after: The imperial carriage was turned back; without hosts like those of Duke Wen of Jin, the dynasty, tethered to the mulberry roots, moreover relied on Lord Tao Kan's strength.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 反我皇駕 is a restoration that happened, and 且賴 marks additional reliance on Tao Kan; the current English turns both into a contrary-to-fact that inverts 且賴.

decisions.reason: 二人斛 is a two-person ration of one hu, so the original “a hu … each” invents a per-person grant; the replacement states the rate correctly and keeps the rest of the sentence.
北中郎將 is the office General of the North Gentlemen of the Household; “north gentlemans-household general” is ungrammatical and obscures the title.
The same office 北中郎將 is again rendered with ungrammatical “gentlemans”; the capitalized office name matches the Chinese.
假護軍將軍庾亮節爲征討都督 confers the jie on Yu Liang as campaign commander; “Borrowed Guard General Yu Liang's staff” reverses 假節 into borrowing his staff.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 假護軍將軍庾亮節爲征討都督

decisions.reason: 假驍騎將軍鐘雅節 likewise grants Zhong Ya the jie; the original “Borrowed … Zhong Ya's staff” misreads the same construction.
帥師救京師 is leading troops to relieve the capital; “moved upstream” is not in the Chinese and is correctly removed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 平南將軍溫嶠帥師救京師

decisions.reason: 督護 titles only Wang Yanqi; Deng Yue and Ji Mu are 太守, so plural “Supervisors” wrongly spreads the office across all three.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣督護王愆期、西陽太守鄧嶽、鄱陽太守紀睦爲前鋒

decisions.reason: 峻至于蔣山 names Mount Jiang only; “east of the capital” is an added gloss not present in the annal.
假領軍將軍卞壼節 is a grant of the jie to Bian Kun, not borrowing his staff.
葬明穆皇后于武平陵 records only burial at Wuping; “beside Emperor Ming” is not in the Chinese.
帝哀泣升車 calls him the emperor; “boy sovereign” is an added characterization not in 帝 or 天子.
百官赴焉 points 焉 at the submitted 苑城, not at rejoining Kuang Shu in person.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 賊將匡術以苑城歸順，百官赴焉

decisions.reason: 詔復遭賊郡縣租稅三年 is a three-year tax remission (復); “restored” inverts the fiscal measure.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 詔復遭賊郡縣租稅三年

decisions.after: Eighth month, Liu Yao's generals Liu Yin and others led troops to invade Shi Sheng and halted at Yong (the received surname graph is a corruption of Liu).
decisions.reason: Received 利曜 is the same man as 劉曜 in the surrounding annal (太子毗…劉胤, then 盡滅劉氏); Wikisource keeps 利曜 while the intended surname is 劉, so rendering Li Yao as a separate person is wrong. The proposed literal note cannot keep Chinese graphs in the English replacement.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 八月，利曜將劉胤等帥衆侵石生，次于雍。

decisions.reason: 僭卽皇帝位 is usurping the imperial throne; the sentence does not name Zhao, and “declared himself” softens 僭.
南中郎將 is South Gentlemen of the Household General; “south gentlemans-household general” is ungrammatical.
李雄將李壽 names Li Shou as Li Xiong’s general only; “of Cheng” is an added polity.
張駿稱臣于石勒 does not mention Former Liang; that polity name is interpolated.
西中郎將 should be West Gentlemen of the Household General; “west gentlemans-household general” is ungrammatical.
南中郎將桓宣 is the same office title; “south gentlemans-household general” is ungrammatical.
嗣偽位 is succession to a false throne; “the Zhao throne” replaces 偽 with an unnamed polity.
石弘將石季龍 makes Shi Hu Shi Hong’s general; dropping Shi Hong erases that command relation, and 陷之 is capture rather than a vague “reduced.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 石弘將石季龍使石斌攻郭權于郿，陷之

decisions.reason: 自立爲天王 does not name Zhao; “heavenly king of Zhao” interpolates the polity.
帝親釋奠 is the libation offering; Confucius and a “capping sacrifice” are not in this sentence (capping is 加元服 in the previous unit).

decisions.after: Shi Yu, serving Shi Hu, struck Zhonglu, and Wang Guo, South Gentlemen of the Household General, fell back to defend Xiangyang.
decisions.reason: south gentlemans-household general is ungrammatical, but “General of the Household Gentlemen of the South” scrambles the usual office order of 南中郎將; South Gentlemen of the Household General matches the Chinese and the chapter’s other 中郎將 renderings.
巳下 is 已下 “and those below,” not a given-name element si after Xie Bao.

decisions.after: The cadet branches of the Ji surname were enfeoffed as Wei, a grace recorded in splendor on the Han rolls.
decisions.reason: 宗姬侯衛 is Ji cadets made the Wei marquisate, parallel to later 衛公, not “to guard the Zhou royal house”; “enfeoffed in Wei” is too locative, so the corrected line keeps the original cadet-branch phrasing and reads 侯衛 as enfeoffment as Wei.
The idiomatic sentence should translate the appointment; the 乙/以 collation note is not part of the annal’s meaning and does not belong in the English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 改司徒爲丞相，乙太傅王導爲之

decisions.reason: Wikisource transmits 乙太傅王導爲之; 乙 is the graphic stand-in for 以 “take/use,” so the literal line must read the appointment, not the heavenly-stem yi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 六月，改司徒爲丞相，乙太傅王導爲之。

decisions.reason: 始興公 is Duke of Shixing; Shian misreads 興.
The same 始興公 must be Shixing in the literal line as well.
漢東 is the country east of the Han, not eastern Hanzhong (漢中).
武悼 is the posthumous title Wudao, not “martyr”; the replacement restores that title.
朕 is the emperor’s first-person “I” in the edict; “He” reverses the voice.
母弟 is a younger brother by the same mother, not a maternal uncle (舅).
The literal “mother's younger brother” is English for 舅; 母弟 is uterine younger brother.
常曰白頭公何在 asks where the white-haired lord who was always spoken of is; it does not say the emperor used to see him at court.
敗其將恆于江陽 names the general 恆; dropping the name and guessing 桓 in the idiomatic English is not a translation of this sentence.
The unit is only 石季龍帥衆伐慕容皝，皝大敗之; “The edict closed” and “then” are translator glue.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 石季龍帥衆伐慕容皝，皝大敗之

decisions.reason: 前鋒小督 is one office, junior van commander; repeating “of the van” restates 前鋒 and muddies the title.
討南羌于闐和 is locative 于 plus the place 闐和, not the toponym 于闐 (Khotan).
王擢 is 石季龍將, Shi Hu’s general; “of Zhao” is not in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 敗石季龍將王擢于三交城

decisions.reason: 舅氏當朝，權侔人主 is Yu Bing’s maternal-uncle house dominating court with power rivaling the sovereign; the original literal is ungrammatical and fuses that clause.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自以舅氏當朝，權侔人主

decisions.reason: 反我皇駕 is a restoration that happened, and 且賴陶公之力 is additional actual reliance on Tao Kan; the original contrary-to-fact turns both into a hypothesis and inverts 且賴.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 反我皇駕，不有晉文之師，繫于苞桑，且賴陶公之力

claimRetractions.reason: The claim that Emperor Ming was named in this burial notice exists only in the idiomatic English “beside Emperor Ming”; the Chinese buries Empress Mingmu at Wuping without naming him as an actor.

value.action: named in the English account of Empress Mingmu's burial at Wuping

dateContext.event: Reception date of the burial notice, not his own activity.

claimRetractions.reason: Attestation of Emperor Ming from s0065 was extracted from the English interpolation, not from a name or dated act in the Chinese burial notice.

value.unresolvedReason: Emperor Ming is named only in the idiomatic English of the AD 328 burial of Empress Mingmu; this chunk does not date his own life or activity, so the burial notice cannot supply his Western active date.
value.event: Retrospective naming in a burial notice; not an activity date.

claimRetractions.reason: s0065 does not state that Emperor Ming was father of the reigning emperor; that parentage was inferred from the invented English mention of Emperor Ming at the burial.
The title “the boy sovereign” is created only by the idiomatic English; 帝 and 天子 do not call him a boy.
The personal name Huan (桓) is not written in this unit; the annal names the general 恆, and the Huan alias was created by the idiomatic conjecture.
The textual-variant claim restates the translator’s note that 恆 may stand for 桓; that note is not a fact of s0305, which writes 恆.

value.statement: The annal writes 恆 (Heng); the English note says the graph may stand for 桓 (Huan).

claimRevisions.reason: The received graph 利曜 is a corruption of 劉曜; the name claim should store the intended 劉曜, with the received 利 already recorded as a textual variant.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 八月，利曜將劉胤等帥衆侵石生，次于雍。

claimRevisions.reason: s0124 says only that Shi Le usurped the imperial throne; Zhao is not named, so the polity-association cannot stand as explicit from this unit.
嗣偽位 does not name Zhao, so Shi Hong’s Zhao association is no longer an explicit extraction from this sentence.
自立爲天王 does not name Zhao, so Shi Hu’s Zhao rule cannot remain explicit on this evidence alone.
始興公 is Duke of Shixing, not Shian; the English title on the name claim must follow the toponym.
The noble-title extraction used the same erroneous Shian; the held title is Duke of Shixing (始興公).
